narrative:
The model determined that you have a 56% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the loan amount you requested, the status of your checking account, and your credit history. The high amount of 10,623 DM you asked for was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Approved applicants request an average of only 3,020 DM, so the model saw your substantially larger request as a significant risk factor that pushed the prediction strongly toward denial.

Your checking account status of less than 0 DM was the second most important driver. Only 12.6% of approved applicants have a negative balance, while most maintain positive balances or no account at all. This negative status also increased the likelihood of being classified as bad credit.

Your credit history of having critical or other existing credits worked in your favor and was the only major factor pulling the prediction back toward approval. However, its positive influence was not strong enough to overcome the combined negative effects of the large loan size and your current account status.

To improve your chances on a future application, consider requesting a smaller loan amount that aligns more closely with what successful applicants typically seek, and work on bringing your checking account balance into positive territory before reapplying. (218 words)
